name: Universities Admissions Centre
description: The shared application centre for undergraduate courses in New South Wales and the ACT, with ATAR information and Educational Access Schemes.
caveat: Applying costs a fee, but the Educational Access Scheme for students facing hardship is free to apply for and can lower entry requirements.

name: SISU — Sistema de Seleção Unificada
description: Brazil’s unified system for claiming a place at a public university using an ENEM score, free of tuition once you are in.
caveat: Portuguese only. The selection window lasts only a few days each January and places shift by the hour.

name: Ontario Universities’ Application Centre
description: The single application every Ontario university applicant uses, with published deadlines and program listings anyone can browse.
caveat: Browsing programmes and deadlines is free; submitting an application costs a fee per programme.

name: DAAD — Study in Germany
description: The official guide to studying in Germany, where most public universities charge no tuition even to international students.
caveat: No tuition does not mean no cost — you must prove you can cover living expenses to get a student visa.

name: Central Applications Office
description: The single application route to Irish universities and colleges, with points requirements published each year.
caveat: There is an application fee, and the discounted early deadline in January saves money.

name: KUCCPS Student Portal
description: Kenya’s central body placing students into universities and TVET colleges after KCSE results, with cut-off points published.
provider: Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service
caveat: Course revision windows are short and announced after KCSE results — watch the portal, not social media.

name: JAMB — Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board
description: Nigeria’s national admissions board: UTME registration, results and the CAPS portal where university offers are accepted.
provider: Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, Nigeria
caveat: UTME registration carries a fee. Only use jamb.gov.ng — there are many imitation sites charging for free services.

name: Study in NL
description: The official Dutch guide to studying in the Netherlands, including English-taught bachelor’s degrees and realistic cost estimates.

name: Study in Norway
description: Norway’s official portal for international students, covering applications, living costs and which programmes are taught in English.
provider: Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills
caveat: Norway now charges tuition to most students from outside the EU/EEA — check the current rules on this page before assuming it is free.

name: College Navigator
description: The federal statistics agency’s college search: admission rates, majors offered, campus safety and net price for every US institution.
caveat: Plainer and less marketed than commercial college search sites — and it sells nothing and collects nothing.

name: CollegePoint
description: Free virtual college advising from trained advisers for high-achieving students from families earning under about $80,000 a year.
caveat: Eligibility is based on grades, test scores and family income — check the criteria before signing up.

name: Matriculate
description: Pairs high-achieving students from low-income families with trained college students who guide them through applications for free.
caveat: Students are usually recruited through partner high schools — ask your counsellor whether your school is one.

name: Jobs and Skills Australia
description: Australian government labour-market data: which occupations are in shortage, what they pay and where the jobs actually are.

name: alis — Alberta Learning Information Service
description: One of the strongest free career sites in Canada: occupational profiles with local wages, plus tools for planning a career change.
caveat: Wage and demand data is Alberta-specific, though the occupational profiles are useful anywhere in Canada.

name: Prospects
description: The UK’s main graduate careers service: what you can do with each degree, job profiles and a free careers quiz.

name: National Career Service
description: India’s government portal for career guidance, free skills training listings and job matching across states.

name: HEART/NSTA Trust
description: Jamaica’s national training agency, offering free and subsidised vocational qualifications to school leavers and adults.

name: AmeriCorps
description: Paid national service terms that come with a Segal Education Award you can put toward college or use to repay student loans.
caveat: The living allowance is modest — the education award and experience are the real return. Some programmes provide housing.

name: Job Corps
description: Free career training, a high school diploma and housing for young people aged 16 to 24, funded by the federal government.
caveat: Residential programme with rules and an application process. Centre availability has changed in recent years — confirm the nearest one is operating.

name: YouthBuild
description: Programmes where young people who left school earn a diploma while learning construction and other trades, and get paid to do it.
caveat: Delivered by local grantees — availability depends entirely on your area. Use the programme locator on this page.

name: YouthRules! — Teen Work Rules
description: What hours a teenager may legally work and which jobs are off limits by age — the federal rules, plainly stated.
caveat: State law can be stricter than federal law. Check both before a first job.

name: Services Australia — Families
description: Family Tax Benefit, Parenting Payment, childcare subsidy and the other Australian payments a single parent may be entitled to.

name: Canada Child Benefit
description: A tax-free monthly payment for families raising children under 18, with a calculator to estimate what you would receive.
caveat: You must file a tax return every year to keep receiving it, even with no income.

name: Citizens Advice
description: Free, independent advice on benefits, debt, housing and employment, online and through local offices across England and Wales.

name: Gingerbread
description: The UK charity for single parent families — a free helpline, benefits guidance, and a community of other single parents.

name: Turn2us
description: A free benefits calculator and a searchable database of charitable grants for families in financial hardship in the UK.

name: Citizens Information
description: Ireland’s official plain-English guide to social welfare, education, housing and family rights, with a free phone service.
Dial 2-1-1 free from anywhere in the US to reach a real person who will find food, rent help, utilities or childcare near you.
caveat: The single best first call when a family is in crisis and does not know where to start.

name: Benefits.gov
description: A free questionnaire that screens you against more than 1,000 federal and state benefit programmes and tells you what you may qualify for.
caveat: The screener gives you a list to pursue — you still apply to each programme separately.

name: Childcare.gov
description: How to find licensed childcare, check a provider’s inspection record, and get help paying for it in your state.
provider: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services

name: Find Your Local Food Bank
description: Enter a postcode to find the nearest food bank and its pantry partners — no eligibility paperwork at most locations.

name: HUD Find Shelter
description: The federal search for emergency shelter, housing, food and health clinics near an address, run by the housing department itself.
provider: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

name: InsureKidsNow.gov
description: Free or low-cost health and dental coverage for children through Medicaid and CHIP, with state-by-state enrolment details.
caveat: You can apply any time of year — unlike marketplace plans, CHIP and Medicaid have no enrolment window.

name: LawHelp.org
description: Free legal aid organisations and self-help guides by state, covering custody, housing, benefits and school issues.

name: LIHEAP — Help With Energy Bills
description: Federal help paying heating and cooling bills, and emergency assistance when a utility shut-off is threatened.
provider: U.S. Administration for Children and Families
caveat: Funds are administered by states and run out during the year — apply as early in the season as you can.

name: Military OneSource
description: Free counselling, education advising, tax help and relocation support for service members, veterans and their families.
caveat: For military-connected families only, including many veterans within a year of separation.

name: National Center for Homeless Education
description: The rights of students without stable housing under the McKinney-Vento Act — including staying at the same school and getting to it.
caveat: These are legal rights, not favours. A family doubled up with relatives often qualifies and does not know it.

name: National Immigration Legal Services Directory
description: A searchable directory of nonprofit organisations offering free or low-cost immigration legal help, by state and county.
caveat: Only organisations recognised by the Department of Justice are listed — this is how you avoid notario fraud.

name: Office of Child Support Services
description: The federal child support programme: how to open a case, establish parentage and enforce an order, with links to every state agency.
provider: U.S. Administration for Children and Families

name: SNAP — Food Assistance
description: The federal food benefit programme, with a pre-screening tool and a link to every state’s application.
caveat: College students face extra eligibility rules — read the student section before assuming a student cannot qualify.

name: Study Assist
description: The Australian government’s official explanation of HECS-HELP and the other student loans, including what you repay and when.

name: Canada Learning Bond
description: Up to $2,000 the government deposits into an education savings plan for a child from a low-income family — no family contribution required.
caveat: You must open an RESP to receive it, and it can be claimed retroactively up to the child’s 21st birthday. Many families never claim it.

name: Student Aid — Government of Canada
description: The federal hub for Canada Student Grants and Loans, including an estimator and the provincial links you actually apply through.
caveat: You apply through your province or territory, not through this page — it points you to the right one.

name: Beneficios Estudiantiles
description: Chile’s official portal for free tuition (Gratuidad), scholarships and student loans, with one application for all of them.
caveat: Spanish only, and the FUAS application window is short — usually a few weeks in October.

name: ICETEX
description: Colombia’s government agency for student credit and scholarships, including funding for study abroad.
caveat: Spanish only. Most ICETEX support is a loan that must be repaid, not a grant — read the terms.

name: Student Finance — GOV.UK
description: The official route to UK tuition fee loans, maintenance loans and extra grants for students with children or a disability.
caveat: Apply as early as spring — funding is not guaranteed to arrive by term start if you apply late.

name: Student Loan Trust Fund
description: Ghana’s government student loan scheme for students at accredited tertiary institutions, applied for with a Ghana Card.
caveat: This is a loan you repay after graduation. A Ghana Card is required to apply.

name: SUSI — Student Universal Support Ireland
description: Ireland’s single national grant scheme covering student contribution fees and maintenance, with an eligibility reckoner before you apply.
provider: City of Dublin Education and Training Board

name: Students’ Loan Bureau
description: Jamaica’s government student loan agency, funding tuition at approved local and regional tertiary institutions.
caveat: Loans require a guarantor and are repaid after study. Read the guarantor obligations before anyone signs.

name: Higher Education Loans Board
description: Kenya’s national body for student loans, bursaries and scholarships for university and TVET students.
caveat: Loans are repaid with interest starting a year after you finish. The site serves an incomplete certificate chain and some browsers warn — check the address bar reads helb.co.ke before signing in.

name: Becas Benito Juárez
description: Mexico’s national scholarship programme paying a regular stipend to students in upper-secondary and higher education from low-income households.
caveat: Spanish only, and registration opens in announced windows rather than year-round.

name: Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND)
description: Nigeria’s federal student loan scheme covering tuition and an upkeep allowance for students at public tertiary institutions.
caveat: Requires a National Identification Number and JAMB number, and applies only to government-owned institutions.

name: StudyLink
description: New Zealand’s student loans and allowances, including extra support for students who are also parents.
provider: Ministry of Social Development, New Zealand

name: College Affordability and Transparency Center
description: The federal site listing the highest- and lowest-cost colleges and linking to every institution’s required net price calculator.
caveat: Sticker price is not what most families pay — use the net price calculator link for each school before ruling it out.

name: Federal Loan Simulator
description: Shows what a federal student loan will actually cost each month under every repayment plan, before you borrow or when you already have.
caveat: You can run it without logging in by entering estimated amounts — useful for a family deciding how much to borrow.

name: GI Bill Comparison Tool
description: Compares what veterans’ education benefits are worth at a specific school, including housing allowance and Yellow Ribbon funding.
caveat: Benefits can transfer to a spouse or child — worth checking even if the student never served.

name: Maryland State Financial Aid
description: Every state grant and scholarship a Maryland student can claim, including need-based awards and programmes for students in foster care.
caveat: Maryland residents only. The state deadline is 1 March and is separate from any federal deadline.

name: Paying for College
description: Plain-language tools from the US consumer regulator for comparing aid offers, understanding loan terms and avoiding predatory student lending.

name: BLS Public Data API
description: Programmatic access to US wage, employment and occupational projection series — the numbers behind every career outlook claim.
caveat: Registering for a key raises your daily limit. Call it during your build and ship the result — a key in browser code is a key you have published.

name: College Scorecard Data and API
description: The full federal dataset on every US college — cost, completion, debt and post-graduation earnings — as bulk files and an API.
caveat: The API needs a free api.data.gov key, so use it in a build step. The bulk CSV files need no key at all and are the better route for a static site.

name: IPEDS — Use the Data
description: The census of American higher education: every institution’s enrolment, staffing, finances and graduation rates, downloadable in full.

name: O*NET Database Downloads
description: The complete occupational database — skills, tasks, knowledge and work styles for roughly 900 occupations — as flat files.
caveat: Free to reuse commercially with attribution. Download the text or Excel files rather than scraping the site.

name: U.S. Census Data API
description: Population, income, poverty and educational attainment data down to neighbourhood level, useful for showing families local context.
caveat: Fetch at build time. Cross-origin calls from a page under a strict CSP will be blocked.

name: Eurostat Education and Training Database
description: Comparable education statistics across every EU country — attainment, early leavers, tertiary enrolment and spending.

name: OECD Education GPS
description: Country-by-country education indicators from the OECD, including PISA results and the earnings premium of a degree.

name: World Bank Education Statistics
description: Education indicators for almost every country on earth, downloadable as CSV and available through a free open API.
caveat: The API needs no key and permits CORS, but fetch it at build time anyway so the page keeps working if the API is down.

name: date-fns
description: Date maths without a heavy dependency — the practical way to build an admissions deadline countdown that is correct in every timezone.

name: decimal.js
description: Arbitrary-precision arithmetic. If you are building a cost or loan calculator, this is how you avoid floating-point money errors.

name: Fuse.js
description: Fuzzy search that runs entirely in the browser, so a resource directory stays searchable with no server and no tracking.

name: Oppia
description: An open-source platform of free interactive lessons, built by a nonprofit for learners without access to a teacher.
caveat: Using oppia.org needs nothing but a browser; self-hosting the platform requires a backend.

name: Papa Parse
description: A fast CSV parser — the piece that turns a government bulk data download into something a static site can actually use.

name: React Aria
description: Accessible, unstyled React behaviour hooks — keyboard and screen reader support done properly, with your own visual design on top.

name: Becas Progresar
description: Argentina’s national scholarship programme paying a monthly stipend to students aged 16–24 who are finishing secondary school or studying at university.
caveat: Spanish only, and applications open in defined windows each year — check the dates before you plan around it.

name: ProUni — Programa Universidade para Todos
description: Brazil’s federal programme granting full and half scholarships at private universities to low-income students, based on their ENEM exam score.
caveat: Portuguese only. You must have sat the ENEM exam in the previous year to apply.

name: Loran Scholars Foundation
description: Canada’s largest four-year undergraduate award, chosen on character and service rather than grades alone, with mentorship and summer programmes attached.
caveat: Deadline falls in the autumn of the final year of high school — much earlier than most Canadian applications.

name: Schulich Leader Scholarships
description: Large STEM entrance scholarships at partner universities in Canada and Israel. Students are nominated by their high school rather than applying directly.
caveat: You cannot apply on your own — ask your school counsellor about being nominated, early.

name: National Scholarship Portal
description: India’s single government portal for central and state scholarships, covering school and college students, with one application shared across schemes.
caveat: Requires an Aadhaar-linked account and a bank account in the student’s own name. Application windows close firmly.

name: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
description: Scholarships for Native American and Alaska Native students at tribal colleges and at any accredited college, through one shared application.

name: APIA Scholars
description: Scholarships for Asian and Pacific Islander American students, including a general programme open to first-year college students with financial need.

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
description: A $20,000 achievement scholarship for 150 graduating high school seniors each year, judged on leadership and service rather than need.
caveat: The application opens in August and closes in late September of senior year — earlier than almost everything else.

name: Dell Scholars Program
description: A scholarship built around students who have overcome real obstacles, adding a laptop, textbook credits and ongoing support rather than money alone.
caveat: You must already be in a participating college-readiness programme to be eligible — check the list before you invest time in the application.

name: Foster Care to Success Scholarships
description: Scholarships and care packages for students who spent time in foster care, from the oldest national nonprofit working with foster youth in college.

name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund
description: Scholarships plus career and mentoring support for students of Hispanic heritage, from high school seniors through graduate school.

name: Horatio Alger Association Scholarships
description: Need-based scholarships for students who have faced and overcome significant adversity, with national and state-level awards each year.

name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation Scholarships
description: Among the largest scholarships in the country for high-achieving students with financial need, including awards for high school seniors and community college transfers.

name: Point Foundation Scholarships
description: Scholarships, mentorship and community for LGBTQ students, including a programme aimed specifically at graduating high school seniors.

name: QuestBridge National College Match
description: Matches high-achieving students from low-income families with full four-year scholarships at some of the most selective colleges in the country.
caveat: The Match application is due in late September of senior year and a match is binding — read the commitment carefully before ranking colleges.

name: The Gates Scholarship
description: A last-dollar scholarship covering the full unmet cost of college for 300 exceptional Pell-eligible minority high school seniors each year.
caveat: Extremely selective and the application closes in September of senior year. Treat it as one option among many, never the plan.

name: Thurgood Marshall College Fund Scholarships
description: Scholarships for students attending publicly supported Historically Black Colleges and Universities, alongside career and internship programmes.
caveat: Most awards require that you attend one of the member HBCUs — check the school list first.

name: UNCF Scholarships
description: One application connecting students to dozens of scholarship programmes from the United Negro College Fund, for HBCUs and other accredited colleges.

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
description: Full scholarships with mentoring for young people from Africa and other under-served regions, delivered through partner universities worldwide.
caveat: You apply to a partner university, not to the Foundation. Start from the partner list on this page.

name: NPTEL
description: Thousands of free university-level engineering and science courses recorded by the Indian Institutes of Technology.
caveat: Watching is free; a proctored certificate requires an in-person exam and an exam fee.

name: SWAYAM
description: India’s national platform for free online courses from class 9 through post-graduate level, with credits transferable at some universities.
caveat: Courses are free; certification requires a paid proctored exam.

name: Code.org
description: Free computer science courses from first steps through AP level, used in tens of thousands of schools, with no cost to families.

name: DigitalLearn
description: Short, patient courses on basic computer and internet skills, built by public librarians for adults who never had the chance to learn.

name: GCFGlobal
description: Free tutorials on everything from Microsoft Word and email to reading a payslip and job hunting, written for absolute beginners.

name: NASA STEM Engagement
description: Free NASA lessons, activities and student challenges across every science subject, usable at home as well as in a classroom.

name: Smithsonian Learning Lab
description: Millions of digitised museum objects and ready-made lessons from the Smithsonian, free to browse and build with.
caveat: Browsing is open; saving your own collections needs a free account.

name: Kolibri
description: A free offline learning platform you install on a laptop and use with no internet at all, bundled with open course libraries.
caveat: You install and run it yourself — built for places with unreliable internet, not a website you simply visit.

name: Project Gutenberg
description: Over 70,000 books whose copyright has expired, free to download in full — including most of the literature on a school reading list.

name: BBC Bitesize
description: Free revision material for GCSEs, Nationals and A-levels, organised by subject and exam board, from the BBC.
caveat: Built around the UK curriculum and exam boards — useful worldwide for the subject explanations, less so for exam formats.

name: National Testing Agency
description: The official source for India’s national entrance exams including JEE and NEET — syllabus, past papers and mock tests.
caveat: Use only nta.ac.in and the official exam sites it links to. Coaching sites impersonating NTA are common.

name: CK-12 Foundation
description: Free adaptive practice and interactive textbooks for maths and science, aligned to US school standards, from a long-running nonprofit.
caveat: You can read everything without an account; saving progress requires a free login.

name: March2Success
description: Free standardised-test practice and study plans covering maths, English and science, with full-length practice tests.
caveat: Run by the U.S. Army as a recruiting-adjacent programme. It is genuinely free with no obligation, but expect that the Army may contact you.

name: OpenStax
description: Peer-reviewed college textbooks, free to read online or download as PDFs, covering the courses most first-year students take.
caveat: Printed copies cost money; the digital versions are permanently free with no account.

name: Beyond Blue
description: Australian mental health support for anxiety and depression, with a 24/7 phone and chat service and resources written for parents.

name: headspace
description: Australia’s national youth mental health service for 12–25 year olds, free in person at local centres and online.
provider: headspace National Youth Mental Health Foundation
caveat: Not the meditation app of a similar name — this is the Australian health service.

name: Kids Help Phone
description: Canada’s 24/7 e-mental health service for young people — call, text or chat, free and anonymous, in English and French.

name: Samaritans
description: Free 24-hour listening support on 116 123 for anyone in distress in the UK and Ireland, with no referral and no waiting list.

name: YoungMinds
description: UK charity for young people’s mental health, including a free Parents Helpline for adults worried about a child.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Call or text 988 from anywhere in the US, any hour, to reach a trained crisis counsellor free and confidentially.
caveat: If someone is in immediate danger, call 988 or 911 now rather than reading further.

name: Child Mind Institute
description: Clinician-written guides for parents on anxiety, ADHD, depression and behaviour — the family reference library, free to read.

name: Crisis Text Line
description: Text HOME to 741741 to reach a trained volunteer crisis counsellor — free, 24/7, and silent, which matters for a teenager.

name: FindTreatment.gov
description: The federal search for mental health and substance use treatment, filterable by what a facility charges and what insurance it takes.
provider: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

name: Mental Health America Screening Tools
description: Free, anonymous, clinically validated mental health screenings for depression, anxiety and more, with results explained.
caveat: A screening is not a diagnosis. It is a starting point for a conversation with a clinician.

name: NAMI — Kids, Teens and Young Adults
description: Guidance from the largest US grassroots mental health organisation for young people and the families supporting them.

name: The Jed Foundation
description: Emotional health support built specifically around the transition from high school to college — for the student and the parent.

name: The National Domestic Violence Hotline
description: Free 24/7 confidential support by phone, chat or text for anyone experiencing abuse, with safety planning help.
caveat: The site has a quick-exit button. If a device may be monitored, use a different one or call 1-800-799-7233.

name: The Trevor Project
description: Free 24/7 crisis support for LGBTQ young people by phone, chat and text, plus resources written for their parents.

name: Befrienders Worldwide
description: A directory of emotional support helplines in more than 30 countries — the fastest way to find a crisis line outside the US.
